newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air India to follow Lufthansa cargo rate rise lead.
newsitem.headline: Air India to follow Lufthansa cargo rate rise lead.

text.p: Air India plans to match the Lufthansa Cargo rates hike on routes to India from mid-January, its cargo service manager Germany, Wolfgang Scholinz, said.
He added that he welcomed the Lufthansa decision to raise cargo prices by 15-70 percent on Germany-India sectors from January 1 and approval would now be sought in Bombay for a similar increase.

"We will definitely support this. We are very happy that someone is making a move towards better rates because no-one could make money at the current levels," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"Once we have a reply from Bombay we will probably follow the national carrier exactly as we normally do. It will probably be from January 15," he said.

Scholinz said market rates to India from Germany had fallen to as low as 1.30-1.35 marks per kilo for the two gateways, Bombay and Delhi, with rates to other destinations up to 50 pfennigs more expensive.
"Prices to India have fallen massively through over-capacity and people have lowered rates to try to break even," he said.
But additional capacity brought onto the market by European carriers earlier in the year, including new Boeing 747 freighter services, had been reduced this autumn, Scholinz noted.
This development and increased market demand for India during the peak autumn season had created a window of opportunity to raise rates.
"Demand for India is very high at present. We are turning away 20 tonnes a day and the same is true for the market in general," he added.
